record.what_it_does: Work management platform for boards, items, and workflows across teams.
record.auth_notes: There are two ways in. (1) A personal API token goes in the Authorization header and mirrors the user's UI permissions. (2) OAuth app tokens are limited by scopes. In the legacy OAuth flow, tokens never expire and there are no refresh tokens. A newer OAuth 2.1 flow adds expiring access tokens, refresh tokens and revocation. The hosted MCP also supports dynamic client registration. A multi-user toolkit would use OAuth.
record.access_notes: A free developer account gives an API token for testing. OAuth apps don't have to be listed or reviewed in the marketplace. Developers can share a public install link with anyone. Unlisted apps show a banner saying monday.com hasn't vetted them, and users must install the app (force_install_if_needed helps with this). Daily API call limits depend on the plan: Free 200, Standard/Basic 1,000, Pro/Trial 10,000, Enterprise 25,000. Free and trial accounts also get lower complexity budgets per minute.
record.api_breadth_notes: A single GraphQL endpoint at https://api.monday.com/v2 covers boards, items, columns, groups, updates, webhooks, users, workspaces, docs and more. I did not count operations. The official MCP exposes more than 60 tools built on this API, according to search summaries.
record.mcp_notes: The vendor hosts a Platform MCP at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp. It uses Streamable HTTP, according to search summaries; SSE is deprecated. You can authenticate with an API token, your own OAuth app, or dynamic client registration. There is also an open-source local package, @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp (github.com/mondaycom/mcp).
record.blocker_notes: Nothing blocks a build. The public GraphQL API, free developer tokens and OAuth are all available. OAuth apps can be shared without marketplace review, but they show an "unvetted" banner. The Free plan's limit of 200 calls a day could restrict end users on free accounts.
